gi2_herzl.topic: Herzl's diaries: the Hechler frontier entry and the 1898 Euphrates note

claims.text: Pipes (MEQ, Spring 1994): 'In 1898, Herzl planned to ask the Ottoman sultan for a territory stretching from the Egyptian frontier to the Euphrates', citing Herzl, Zionistische Tagebücher 1895-1899, ed. Wachten, Harel et al. (Berlin: Ullstein, 1983), vol. 2, p. 650.
Pipes: 'Herzl did not in fact request the Nile-to-Euphrates region from the Ottoman king or anyone else'; 'Four years later he spoke of settling Jews in Mesopotamia.'

Pipes on myths: the Knesset 'Euphrates to the Nile' inscription claim (Al-Jazira, 17 Jan 1982) - 'no one has yet laid eyes on' it; Arafat's flag-stripes claim (Playboy, Sept 1988) - the blue lines derive from the prayer shawl; the 10-agora coin patterned on a coin of 37 BCE.

Herzl's diary (Complete Diaries, 1960, vol. I, p. 342, as quoted by Wikipedia) records Hechler unfolding maps of Palestine: 'The northern frontier ought to be the mountains facing Cappadocia; the southern, the Suez Canal. The slogan to be circulated: "The Palestine of David and Solomon!"'
H.S. Haddad (Journal of Palestine Studies 3:4, 1974) wrote that Hechler 'gave Herzl the biblical definitions of the boundaries' (as quoted by Wikipedia).

Chamberlain judged Cyprus, Sinai and El-Arish impractical (inhabited or not under British control) but agreed to discuss El-Arish with Lansdowne; he suggested East Africa (modern Kenya); the Sixth Zionist Congress (Basel, 1903) voted 295 to 178 to send a fact-finding group; the plan was rejected in 1905 and the British withdrew the offer.

gi2_map1919.topic: Zionist Organization statement and boundary proposal at Paris, 3 Feb 1919; the Mandate lines as settled 1920-23

claims.text: ZO Statement on Palestine presented to the Paris Peace Conference 3 Feb 1919; signed for the ZO by Walter Rothschild, Nahum Sokolow, Chaim Weizmann; for the ZOA by Julian Mack, Stephen Wise, Harry Friedenwald, Jacob De Haas, Mary Fels, Louis Robison, Bernard Flexner; Israel Rosoff for the Russian ZO.
Resolution: 'The High Contracting Parties recognize the historic title of the Jewish people to Palestine'.

Boundaries: 'The boundaries of Palestine shall follow the general lines set out below': north from 'a point on the Mediterranean Sea in the vicinity south of Sidon', Lebanon foothill watersheds, Hermon slopes, east past Beit Jenn to Nahr Mughaniye; east 'a line close to and west of the Hedjaz Railway terminating in the Gulf of Akaba'; south 'a frontier to be agreed upon with the Egyptian Government'; west the Mediterranean; details to a Special Commission with Jewish representation.

Justification: 'The economic life of Palestine, like that of every other semi-arid country, depends on the available water supply'; Hermon is 'Palestine's real "Father of Waters"'; riparian rights of 'the people dwelling south of the Litani River' by international arrangement; 'The fertile plains east of the Jordan' linked with the west; free access to the Hedjaz Railway; Gulf of Akaba ports.

The statement does not use the word 'Arab'; it says 'nothing shall be done which may prejudice the civil and religious rights of existing non-Jewish communities in Palestine' and calls for safeguarding 'the established rights of the present non-Jewish population'.

Franco-British Convention signed Paris 23 Dec 1920 placed the bulk of the Golan in the French sphere; commission final report 3 Feb 1922 moved the line to include the entire Sea of Galilee and Yarmuk valley in Palestine; approved 7 March 1923.
League Council approved the Transjordan memorandum on 16 Sept 1922, excluding Transjordan from the Mandate's articles concerning a Jewish national home (Article 25 allowed exclusion).

gi2_bothbanks.topic: Jabotinsky, the Revisionists, Betar, the song and the Irgun emblem: 'both banks of the Jordan'

claims.text: 'The founding conference of the Union of Zionists-Revisionists took place in Paris in 1925'; aim of a Jewish majority 'on both sides of the Jordan'; to 'reestablish the Jewish Legion'; Jabotinsky's 1931 resolution aimed to make the whole Mandatory territory including Transjordan a Jewish state (Shavit); secession from the WZO 1935 after a plebiscite; the NZO 'opposed and combated the partition of Palestine as proposed in 1937'; Irgun veterans founded Herut in Oct 1948; a separate Revisionist list won 0.7% in the First Knesset.
EJ: the Revisionist movement 'hotly opposed the separation of Transjordan'; slogan 'a Jewish state on both sides of the Jordan'.

'The Iron Wall' dated 4 Nov 1923: 'Zionist colonisation must either stop, or else proceed regardless of the native population'; 'behind an iron wall, which the native population cannot breach'; 'the only way to reach an agreement in the future is to abandon all idea of seeking an agreement at present'; 'I am prepared to take an oath binding ourselves and our descendants' ... 'never try to eject anyone'; 'The Ethics of the Iron Wall' published in Rassviet (Paris) 11 Nov 1923.
Betar founded 1923 in Riga by Jabotinsky; 'In 1934, Poland was home to 40,000 of Betar's 70,000 members'.

Jabotinsky wrote 'The East Bank of the Jordan' in 1929 while visiting Paris; first version given to the Kaunas students' union 'Yardeniya' on 18 Nov 1929; known version published in Do'ar HaYom on 11 April 1930; became one of the best-known songs of Betar; refrain: the Jordan has two banks and both are claimed.

Irgun operated 1931-1948, began as a breakaway from the Haganah; emblem a hand holding a rifle over a map of Mandatory Palestine and Transjordan with the motto 'only thus'; policy based on Revisionist Zionism; Jabotinsky its commander until his death in 1940; Begin led it 1943-48; political predecessor to Herut and later Likud.

gi2_peel.topic: Peel partition map 1937, Zionist and Arab responses, Woodhead; Ben-Gurion's letter to Amos and the disputed sentence

claims.text: Peel (July 1937): Jewish state of the coastal strip from Mount Carmel south to Be'er Tuvia, the Jezreel Valley and Galilee, roughly 17%; Arab state about 75% (hills of Judea and Samaria, the Negev) united with Transjordan; a mandate zone of about 8% between Jaffa and Jerusalem.

EJ: Peel Jewish state 'the whole of Galilee and the Jezreel Valley', most of Beth-Shean valley, coastal plain from the Lebanese border to Be'er Tuviyyah; British zone Jerusalem, Bethlehem, corridor to Jaffa, Nazareth; 20th Congress called the scheme 'unacceptable' but authorised the Executive to negotiate, any arrangement to go to a newly elected Congress; Woodhead found Peel 'impracticable'.
Twentieth Zionist Congress, Zurich, 3-16 Aug 1937: rejected the plan 'because it sees the projected Jewish state as too small' and chose to keep negotiating over borders.
Arab Higher Committee: 'Partition would create in Palestine two neighboring hostile states'.
Cmd. 5893 (Nov 1938): the Partition Commission advised 'unanimously against the adoption of the scheme of partition outlined by the Royal Commission'; government found partition impracticable.

Ben-Gurion letter to Amos, 5 Oct 1937; handwritten original in the IDF Archive; translation published by the Institute for Palestine Studies; 'The establishment of a state, even if only on a portion of the land' ... 'a powerful boost to our historical endeavors to liberate the entire country'; partition 'not the end but the beginning'; Arabs 'already have an abundance of deserts but not of manpower, financial resources, or creative initiative'.

Disputed sentence: Morris (1988) quoted Teveth's English (1985) 'We must expel Arabs and take their places'; several words crossed out in the original; Karsh (2000) argued restoring them reverses the meaning; Morris called the focus 'nothing more than (an essentially mendacious) red herring' and said Ben-Gurion endorsed transfer 'either voluntarily or by compulsion' (Commentary 2011).
Karsh's reading of the original: 'We do not wish and do not need to expel Arabs and take their place.'

Morris: consulted the original; words crossed out leaving 'We must expel the Arabs'; others suggested a later hand and a restored reading 'We must not expel the Arabs'; Ben-Gurion 'rarely made corrections'; later dropped the quote or used the version the restoration allows.
Pappé (2006) quotation 'The Arabs will have to go, but one needs an opportune moment for making it happen, such as a war': punctuation error acknowledged by JPS in 2012.

Ben-Gurion at the Jewish Agency executive, June 1938, as quoted by Masalha (1992, p.107) and Segev (2000, p.403): 'we will abolish the partition of the country and we will expand to the whole Land of Israel' - secondary; protocol not checked.
